chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding the prayer of the two Eids, he said: He should exclaim Takbir, then recite, then exclaim five [Takbirs], and perform Qunut between every two Takbirs. Then he should exclaim the seventh Takbir and bow with it. Then he should prostrate, then stand for the second [rak'ah], so he should recite, then exclaim four [Takbirs], and perform Qunut between every two Takbirs. Then he should exclaim Takbir and bow with it.

key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: Prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are performed in each rak'ah of the Eid prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific ritual structure of the Eid prayer, emphasizing the five Takbirs in the first rak'ah and four in the second, with Qunut recited between each pair. This method aligns with the prominent Shia juristic view, distinguishing it from other schools by its consistent placement of supplication, thereby reinforcing the prayer's role as a communal act of gratitude and spiritual elevation. The hadith serves as a foundational legal text for understanding the procedural nuances of this annual celebration in Shia jurisprudence.
